claims.criterion: Supported if each step of the two proofs is checked and follows; refuted if a step fails or a consistent additive rule with a non-constant weight is exhibited.
claims.label: A
claims.text: A family of set functions on the walks of each length of a gain digraph is one function on cylinder sets of histories exactly when it is consistent under continuation, and an additive switching-invariant rule that is consistent under continuation is a multiple of the number of walks (paper G10, Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 4.1).

claims.criterion: Supported if each step of the two proofs is checked and follows; refuted if a step fails or a consistent rule other than the square is exhibited on these carriers.
claims.label: B
claims.text: On the signed arc digraph of the line a rule adding over end vertices a function of the modulus of the summed gains is consistent under continuation only for the square, and on a norm-preserving gain digraph with a merging pair of walks the only consistent power is the second (paper G10, Theorems 5.1 and 5.2).

claims.criterion: The comparison command exits 0 and the counts read from the result files are 26, 19 and 7.
claims.label: C
claims.text: The six programs of the fourth session, rerun in a fresh directory, reproduce their six result files byte for byte, with 26 predicates of which 19 pass and 7 fail and are kept.

claims.criterion: Supported by a construction with a stated limit and an error estimate; refuted by a proof that no arrangement of gains of bounded order has such a limit.
claims.label: D
claims.text: Gains of bounded order (in particular the orders 2, 3, 4, 6) can produce the rays of a weak force in a controlled limit (open problem OP-28, favourable reading).

claims.criterion: Supported by a proved bound; the computed instances alone leave it unresolved; refuted if the remainder fails to decrease in the instances.
claims.label: E
claims.text: Under a linear gain the centroid of a packet follows the packet-averaged ray displaced by the connection of the branch eigenvector, with a remainder of first order in the field (paper G10, Section 7).

claims.criterion: Supported only if every gate of the program's gate map is met by the trials; not identified if a checked non-selection witness shows the assumptions admit a classical or otherwise different rule on the same carrier.
claims.label: F
claims.text: With events taken as sets of histories, the constructed trials GH-1 and GH-2 yield quantum mechanics and classical mechanics (the target of the program, as a claim about these trials).

body.label: Z4
body.title: Director Z fourth session: histories as events, order of the rule, forces from gains of bounded order, ray remainder

body.extent: all of it, 9 pages; written by this participant in this session

extracted and verified (967 files); read in full: program charter, standards, registers of open problems, gate map and bridge candidates, Director Z records of three sessions, sources of papers G7, G8, G9; not read: the other 37 papers, the packets of Directors A, B and G beyond the adjudication registers

body.text: That events are sets of histories is itself an assumption about the event structure; the lemma converts the requirement of paper G9 into that assumption and does not derive it.

The theorems cover only rules that add over end vertices a function of one modulus; rules outside that form are not classified, and with trivial gains the count is consistent on the same digraph, so the second order is forced only for a rule that depends on the gains on a branching norm-preserving carrier.
The proofs were written and checked by the same participant; the executed predicates (M1 and its controls, S1) test instances of the conclusion, not the proofs.

body.how: Accepted. Claim A is the equivalence and the exclusion that follows from it; that events are sets of histories is listed as supplied in paper G10, Section 8 (1), and in the ledger of the constructed trials.

Accepted and stated in paper G10: Section 5 closes with the division between the count, which is consistent with trivial gains, and the square; Section 8 (6) lists rules outside the form as not classified. The claim as posed is confined to that form and those carriers.
Stands. No second participant examined the proofs. The executed predicates test instances of the conclusions by a route that does not use the proofs.

body.left_open: Mathematics only; proofs by this participant, unrefereed. Predicate S3 (linear consistency equations on three gain graphs) agrees. The assumption that events are sets of histories is supplied.

Mathematics only; proofs by this participant, unrefereed. Predicates M1 with two rejecting controls and one accepting control, and S1 (exhaustive over 255 events), agree. Rules outside the stated form are not classified. The reference of Li and So was not inspected and is not used in the proof.
The check is this participant's report; no host observed the command. Seven failed predicates are kept: S5 (two), C1, C1b, M1 and L3 of the first program for modulus rules, E1.

Proved: an exact translation of the quasi-momentum by Phi needs gains of order at least 2 pi / Phi; for orders 3 and above no quasi-energy lies in all local spectra except four band edges for order 4. Observed: staircases of order 3, 4, 6 confine, leak or are strong fields; an order-4 staircase reaches 0.69, 0.54 and 0.16 of the mean-field displacement at block lengths 16, 64, 256. Not decided: a dynamical theorem for winding gains of bounded order; arrangements other than staircases.

No bound is proved. Instances: remainder 0.0735 to 0.0016 site over periods 64 to 2048, fitted exponent -1.1. The remainder for the ray through the central quasi-momentum does not decrease (predicate E1 failed and is kept). The theorem of Panati, Spohn and Teufel concerns Schroedinger operators and was read in its abstract, introduction and statement of Theorem 3 only.

Non-selection witnesses, checked: on the same digraph with trivial gains the count is consistent under continuation (control of M1), so the event structure admits a classical rule; real gains satisfy every statement, so complex amplitudes are not selected; the carrier, the form of the rule, the group and the character are supplied. No gate of the gate map is passed.

body.note: Each claim has a finding; one objection is recorded open (no second participant).

The principal directed that no question or note be addressed to them during the work; the findings are released in the edition and in the closing summary of the session.
